items.followUp: Write any two functions of the kidneys.

rubric.why: Bile production is a major function of the liver.
rubric.description: Names bile production as one liver function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the liver produces bile.

rubric.why: Any one additional correct function is sufficient.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any correct function other than bile production.

modelAnswer: The liver produces bile, which helps in the digestion of fats.
The liver also detoxifies harmful substances in the blood.

items.followUp: Define the terms heartbeat and pulse.

rubric.why: Systole is the contraction phase of the heart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying heart contraction, with or without mentioning blood being pumped out.

rubric.why: Diastole is the relaxation phase of the heart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying heart relaxation, with or without mentioning filling with blood.

modelAnswer: Systole is the phase in which the heart muscle contracts and pumps blood out of the heart.
Diastole is the phase in which the heart muscle relaxes and its chambers fill with blood.

items.followUp: What is a blood transfusion, and why is blood-group matching necessary?

rubric.why: Agglutination is the clumping of red blood cells following an antigen–antibody reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that red blood cells clump together, usually due to an antigen–antibody reaction.

rubric.why: Angioplasty opens or widens a narrowed or blocked blood vessel.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that angioplasty widens or opens a narrowed or blocked artery, typically using a balloon catheter.

modelAnswer: Agglutination is the clumping together of red blood cells when incompatible blood groups react due to antigens and antibodies.
Angioplasty is a procedure used to widen a narrowed or blocked artery, usually by inserting and inflating a balloon catheter.

items.followUp: Name the four ABO blood groups and state what determines a person's ABO group.

rubric.why: Blood groups are classified according to the antigens present or absent on red blood cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining it as a classification of blood based on red-cell antigens.

rubric.why: These are the four groups in the ABO system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for listing A, B, AB and O.

modelAnswer: The blood group system classifies blood according to the presence or absence of specific antigens on red blood cells.
The four blood groups are A, B, AB and O.

items.followUp: Explain how biology is related to chemistry and mathematics.

rubric.why: Biophysics applies principles of physics to biological structures and processes.
rubric.description: Explains the relationship between biology and physics.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for naming biophysics and explaining that it applies physics to living organisms or biological processes.

rubric.why: Biochemistry studies the chemical substances and reactions of living organisms.
rubric.description: Explains the relationship between biology and chemistry.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for naming biochemistry and explaining its study of chemicals or chemical reactions in organisms.

rubric.why: Other sciences also provide methods for studying biological data and the distribution or use of organisms.
rubric.description: Gives another valid biological connection with a science.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example such as biomathematics, biogeography or bioeconomics, with an appropriate explanation where needed.

modelAnswer: Biology is linked with physics in biophysics, which applies physical principles to living organisms and their processes.
Biology is linked with chemistry in biochemistry, which studies the chemical substances and reactions occurring in organisms.
Biomathematics uses mathematical and statistical methods to analyse biological data.
Biogeography studies the geographical distribution of organisms.
Bioeconomics applies economic principles to biological resources and their use.

items.followUp: Describe the main types of white blood cells and state their function.

rubric.why: White blood cells are colourless, nucleated blood cells.
rubric.description: States basic features of white blood cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that white blood cells are colourless and have a nucleus.

rubric.why: White blood cells are grouped into granulocytes and agranulocytes; examples include neutrophils, lymphocytes and monocytes.
rubric.description: Names the main groups or examples of white blood cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the two groups or at least two correct types.

rubric.why: White blood cells protect the body from infection through actions including phagocytosis and antibody production.
rubric.description: Explains the protective functions of white blood cells.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for stating their defence role and explaining a mechanism such as engulfing pathogens or producing antibodies.

modelAnswer: White blood cells, or leucocytes, are colourless blood cells that have a nucleus.
They are classified into granulocytes and agranulocytes; examples include neutrophils, lymphocytes and monocytes.
White blood cells defend the body against disease-causing organisms.
Some engulf pathogens by phagocytosis, while lymphocytes produce antibodies.

items.followUp: Define an endangered species and describe two ways its habitat can be protected in Pakistan.

rubric.why: An endangered species has a population so low that it is at risk of extinction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the species is threatened with extinction or has very low numbers and may become extinct.

rubric.why: Destruction or loss of habitat reduces the places where species can live and reproduce.
rubric.description: Explains habitat destruction as a cause of endangerment.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for identifying habitat loss or deforestation and linking it to declining populations.

rubric.why: Hunting, pollution and other human pressures can further reduce wildlife populations in Pakistan.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for two further valid causes, or one cause explained clearly.

modelAnswer: An endangered species is a species whose population has fallen to such a low level that it is at risk of extinction.
In Pakistan, habitat destruction and deforestation reduce the food, shelter and breeding sites available to wildlife.
Illegal hunting and poaching directly reduce the populations of animals such as markhor and snow leopard.
Pollution and other human activities also damage habitats and threaten species, including aquatic wildlife such as the Indus dolphin.

items.followUp: Compare aerobic and anaerobic respiration in terms of oxygen use, products and energy released.

rubric.why: Aerobic respiration requires oxygen, whereas anaerobic respiration occurs without oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly contrasting the oxygen requirement of the two processes.

rubric.why: Aerobic respiration completely breaks down glucose, while anaerobic products include lactic acid or ethanol and carbon dioxide.
rubric.description: Compares the products or completeness of breakdown.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly giving the products or stating that aerobic breakdown is complete and anaerobic breakdown is incomplete.

rubric.why: Aerobic respiration releases more energy than anaerobic respiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that aerobic respiration releases more energy and anaerobic respiration less.

rubric.why: The processes differ in cellular location, and both break down glucose to release energy.
rubric.description: Adds a further valid difference or shared feature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct location or for stating that both processes break down glucose to release energy.

modelAnswer: Aerobic respiration requires oxygen; anaerobic respiration occurs without oxygen.

Aerobic respiration completely breaks down glucose to carbon dioxide and water, whereas anaerobic respiration incompletely breaks it down, producing lactic acid in muscles or ethanol and carbon dioxide in yeast.
Aerobic respiration releases more energy than anaerobic respiration.
Aerobic respiration mainly occurs in the mitochondria, while anaerobic respiration takes place in the cytoplasm.
